content: Latest Bangladesh Business World Sports Opinion Politics Diplomacy More E-Paper ☀️ 🌐 English বাংলা Russian Hindi Chinese Trending Saudi-Houthi Conflict Tarique Rahman Israel Election Road Accident Mirpur Test × Today's Newspaper Latest World Cup Magazine 2026 Election 2026 Follow Us Print: 29 Oct 2026 Bangladesh Dengue spreads to villages as death toll hits 377 Experts want entomologist-led, scientifically tested mosquito control Hedayet Ullah Khan Published: 25 Oct 2026, 12:00 AM Updated: 25 Oct 2026, 11:07 AM Share Share options Print Copy link Facebook X WhatsApp Linkedin A A Dengue has killed 377 people across the country this year, 132 of them in the first 24 days of October, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), as public health experts say the disease is spreading from cities into districts and rural communities where local authorities lack the capacity to control mosquitoes. Six people died in the 24 hours to 8am on Saturday, while 1,898 patients were admitted to hospitals during the period. Cumulative admissions since 1 January have reached 1,21,699. Two of the latest victims were from Chattogram division, and one each from Dhaka South City Corporation, Khulna division, Mymensingh and Rajshahi division. Dengue claimed 43 lives in August and 148 in September, the highest monthly figure this year, before October’s 132 deaths. Dhaka division, including the two city corporations, has recorded 180 deaths, followed by Khulna (67), Chattogram (37), Mymensingh (31), Barishal (28), Rajshahi (24), Rangpur (7) and Sylhet (3). The DGHS recorded 413 dengue deaths in 2025. Public health experts say the disease is no longer confined to Dhaka and other cities. Prof Dr Be-Nazir Ahmed, public health strategist and former director of Disease Control at Directorate General of Health Services, told the Daily Sun that dengue, once regarded as primarily urban, is becoming established in rural areas. He cited the presence of aedes mosquitoes there and widespread domestic travel, which carries the virus to new areas as infected people move around the country. “Dengue will remain a risk for Bangladesh in the coming days. I believe it will pose an even greater challenge. In particular, it could become a devastating disease in rural areas,” he said. He said union parishads struggle to carry out effective mosquito-control operations, while many municipalities lack the necessary manpower, equipment and institutional capacity. Read More Measles, dengue claim 10 more lives in 24hrs Prevention measures must be set up at union, upazila and municipal levels as well as in major cities, he said, or rising rural infections could become increasingly difficult to manage. Dr Mushtuq Husain, public health expert and advisor to Institute of Epidemiology Disease Control and Research, said dengue has been a major challenge since 2020, with a severe outbreak in 2023. It has now reached remote districts such as Barguna and Satkhira, he said, with human movement carrying the virus to areas where aedes mosquitoes allow local transmission. Be-Nazir Ahmed said aedes mosquitoes generally breed in stagnant clean water around homes, including on rooftops and balconies and in flowerpots, water containers, construction sites and abandoned properties. Water collecting in potholes and open spaces, and poor waste management, also create favourable conditions. Spraying insecticide alone cannot control dengue without addressing these causes, he said, adding that authorities need to identify breeding sites and high-infection areas and base strategies on reliable data. In many areas, mosquito-control drives are held but stagnant water is not regularly removed, he noted. Dr Mushtuq urged authorities to involve entomologists in mosquito-control programmes, saying decisions on which insecticides to use, and how and where to apply them, should rest on scientific assessment. Control workers need proper training, he said, and insecticides should be tested regularly. Authorities must also evaluate whether operations are reducing mosquito populations and transmission, rather than focusing on visible campaigns and publicity. Criticising the government’s approach, he said, “If you tie a horse to a post and whip it, it will run with all its might, but it will not move an inch forward. The government’s approach is much the same.” DGHS age-specific data show that 17,409 patients this year were aged 21 to 25, the highest among the five-year age groups. Another 17,200 were aged 26 to 30 and 16,446 were aged 16 to 20. More than 6,200 children under five were also affected. Dr Mushtuq said young people may be more exposed to aedes mosquitoes because they spend more time outside the home for work and education. Be-Nazir Ahmed pointed to prior infections. There are four main dengue serotypes, and infection with one does not necessarily protect against the others. A later infection with a different serotype can increase the risk of severe dengue in some cases. Older people may have developed immunity to all four through earlier infections, unlike younger people, he said. Read More Cox’s Bazar tourism boom exposes gaps in visitor safety Most patients recover with appropriate care, but some develop complications, including plasma leakage, low blood pressure, severe bleeding and impaired organ function. Health experts said the period when fever subsides is particularly critical, as severe symptoms can develop within 24 to 48 hours. Warning signs include severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding from the nose or gums, unusual weakness, restlessness, breathing difficulties, cold hands and feet, and reduced urine output. Anyone with these symptoms should seek urgent medical attention. Many patients initially mistake dengue for ordinary fever and delay seeking care. Treatment requires fluid management based on the patient’s condition, monitoring of blood pressure and urine output, and necessary tests. Patients should not take excessive fluids or intravenous saline on their own, experts said. Paracetamol may be used for fever under medical guidance, but aspirin, ibuprofen and certain other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs can increase the risk of bleeding and should be avoided unless a qualified physician advises otherwise. Experts said adding beds is not enough. Hospitals must also be able to identify patients whose condition is deteriorating rapidly, through complete blood count tests, haematocrit monitoring, assessment of fluid intake and urine output, and intensive care for severe cases. Not every patient needs admission, they said, as the decision should rest on symptoms and a physician’s assessment, though patients with warning signs need prompt attention. They also called for coordination between public and private hospitals, adequate staffing, access to diagnostic tests, stronger emergency capacity and regularly updated infection and mortality data. Seasonal campaigns alone cannot control dengue, the experts said, calling for year-round efforts to eliminate breeding sites, strengthen surveillance, improve waste management and raise public awareness, even when cases are low. Unless local capacity is strengthened from cities to villages, mosquito control becomes more scientific and patients receive timely treatment, dengue is likely to remain a major public health threat in Bangladesh, they said. (WWSB) - Health officials have confirmed a human case of locally acquired dengue in Manatee County. The Florida Department of Health in Manatee County said it is working with Manatee County Mosquito Control to increase surveillance and prevention efforts. Those efforts include removing mosquito breeding areas and aerial spraying. The confirmation marks a change from earlier this month, when local officials said there were no confirmed locally acquired dengue cases in Manatee County. Local mosquito authorities kicking up protocol midst Dengue Fever surge Health officials are urging residents to take steps to avoid mosquito bites. The Department of Health said it continues statewide monitoring for mosquito-borne illnesses, including dengue, West Nile virus, Eastern equine encephalitis, St. Louis encephalitis, malaria and chikungunya. The advisory did not identify where in Manatee County the person may have been exposed. It also did not provide the patient’s condition, the number of locally acquired cases or details about planned aerial-spraying areas and dates. Residents can report dead birds to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, according to the department. Copyright 2026 WWSB. All rights reserved. No, I am under 18 Yes, I am 18+ Home Info Sehat Dengue Fever Risk Increases During Rainy Season, Know the Causes and Prevention Temukan lebih banyak Berita Aktual Berita Ekonomi Berita Teknologi 28 Oktober 2026, 00:57 | Editorial Team MS Hadi Reporter Tim VOI Editor Illustration (Pixabay/FotoshopTofs) Share: YOGYAKARTA - A number of regions in Indonesia have started to be hit by rain after a long drought. We are grateful that the land can finally be wet again and the forest fires can be extinguished immediately. However, this season change also brings health challenges that should not be ignored, one of which is the increased risk of dengue fever (DBD). Sejarah Indonesia Temukan lebih banyak Baca Isu Politik Pemerintah Cek Layanan This disease transmitted by the bite of the Aedes aegypti mosquito can attack anyone, from children to adults. Therefore, we need to know the causes of the increase in dengue fever cases during the rainy season and what can be done as a preventive measure. The following is a discussion. Why Does Dengue Fever Risk Increase During Rainy Season? There are several factors that increase the risk of dengue fever during the rainy season. Reported from Continental Hospitals, here are some things you need to know. Many Water Stains The main reason why dengue fever spreads faster during the rainy season is none other than the many puddles. We can find puddles in various places, ranging from plant pots, old tires, to clogged water drains. Water that is contained in these places can become a location for Aedes aegypti mosquitoes to lay eggs if the conditions are right. "We must remember, these mosquitoes do not breed in dirty ponds or waterways. They actually need relatively clean water puddles to lay eggs. Mosquito Development is Supported by Environmental Conditions Warm temperatures combined with high humidity during the rainy season support the development of mosquitoes from eggs to adults. When breeding sites are available in large numbers, mosquito populations have the potential to increase in a relatively short time. Mosquito Activity in the Daytime This increased humidity also makes Aedes aegypti mosquitoes more active. This type of mosquito is different from other mosquitoes that generally bite at night. This dengue-carrying mosquito is more active during the day, especially in the morning and afternoon. Therefore, even if you are at home or at work, you are still at risk of being bitten by Aedes mosquitoes. How to Prevent Dengue Fever at Home During Rainy Season Preventing dengue fever is not enough just by maintaining the cleanliness of the house and yard when the rainy season comes. Reported from the same page, here are some steps that can be taken inside and outside the house to prevent dengue transmission. Make Sure There Is No Water Stains Check the home environment at least once a week to ensure there are no containers that can potentially hold water. If there are, empty, brush, cover, or remove the items so that they do not become a place for mosquitoes to lay eggs. Temukan lebih banyak Pemerintahan Cari Peta Wilayah Tur Asia Tenggara You need to pay attention to the containers used daily, such as pet drinking places, water coolers, or plant pot holders. Clean the container regularly and make sure there are no puddles. Use Anti Mosquito Lotion You can use lotion or mosquito repellent products to help reduce the risk of bites while at home and outdoors. Choose products with active ingredients that have been approved by the Ministry of Health and use them according to the instructions on the packaging. Wear Clothes that Cover the Skin When you are outside the house, wear long-sleeved clothes and long pants. You can also use socks and shoes to help reduce the skin that is open to mosquito bites. Although it does not completely eliminate the risk of bites, clothing that covers the skin can be an additional protection. Use Mosquito Net While Sleeping Mosquito nets can help protect family members from mosquito bites while sleeping, including during naps. The use of mosquito nets while sleeping is especially for babies, small children, and the elderly who need more protection during rest. Make sure the mosquito net is properly attached and does not leave gaps that allow mosquitoes to enter. That is a discussion of a number of things you need to know about the increased risk of dengue fever during the rainy season and the prevention measures. By implementing the prevention measures above, you also help reduce the risk of transmission of DBD in the community. If you experience dengue fever symptoms, immediately contact a doctor so that you can get the right treatment immediately. By Kevin Killough Published: October 26, 2026 7:48am Article Dig Deeper Benjamin Jacob, University of South Florida professor, and a team of researchers, are using artificial intelligence to target breeding grounds for mosquitoes carrying the dengue virus in an effort to address an outbreak of dengue fever in Florida. Cases of the disease have spiked this year, where 425 locally acquired cases have been reported. There were an additional 288 international cases reported as well. The outbreak was largely concentrated in Hillsborough County, which surrounds Tampa, The Hill reported. Jacob's system uses satellite images along with weather patterns and known breeding grounds to identify potential locations quickly. The information is then handed over to the state for its eradication efforts. content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, October 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Autoimmune disease linked to greater dengue severity in Colombian cohort by October 26, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Autoimmune disease linked to greater dengue severity in Colombian cohort Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram The study included 171 participants whose outcomes were assessed over 2014–2024: 57 had autoimmune diseases and 114 did not. Severe dengue occurred in 7.0% of the autoimmune-disease group, compared with 2.6% of the comparison group. After adjustment for potential confounders, the association between autoimmune disease and dengue severity was estimated at an odds ratio of 2.14, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.08–4.41 and p = 0.030. The researchers compared demographic, clinical and outcome measures between the two groups and examined laboratory-test trends before, during and after infection. Women represented 87.7% of the sample, and the median age was 48 years. Among participants with autoimmune diseases, rheumatoid arthritis was the most frequent diagnosis at 42%, followed by systemic lupus erythematosus at 29.8% and Sjögren’s syndrome at 19.3%. Patients with autoimmune diseases more often presented with dengue warning signs: these were reported in 66.7% of the autoimmune-disease group and 55.4% of the group without autoimmune diseases. The study also found a higher proportion reporting a previous dengue infection in the autoimmune-disease group, at 49.1% compared with 43.0%. Hospitalization was more frequent among participants with autoimmune disease, at 68.4% versus 61.4%, but that difference was not statistically significant, with p = 0.368. Discover more Check Symptoms Find Treatments Explore Data infection Intensive-care admission was also numerically higher in the autoimmune-disease group, at 12.3% versus 5.3%, although the difference did not reach statistical significance, with p = 0.125. Participants with autoimmune diseases had longer hospital stays, but the supplied research summary does not report the numerical durations. For the severity analysis, the investigators calculated crude and adjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals to identify factors associated with dengue severity. They also performed sensitivity analyses, interaction testing and bootstrap validation, and reported that the findings were consistent across the adjusted, sensitivity and bootstrap analyses. The authors described this consistency as support for the robustness of the association within the dataset. Dengue is an acute viral illness transmitted by the mosquitoes Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus and is prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions. Although most infections are asymptomatic, severe disease can develop, particularly in people with risk factors. The researchers noted that the clinical course of dengue had been studied less extensively in patients with autoimmune diseases and that no prior research on this question had been conducted in Colombia. Larger prospective multicenter studies were needed to confirm the association and clarify its immunopathogenic basis. content: Pasar al contenido principal Main navigation Inicio Áreas y temas Temas prioritarios Grupos estables investigación Ciencias exactas y tecnología Economía, Negocios y Desarrollo Humanidades, artes y disciplinas creativas Persona y Sociedad Salud Integral y Bienestar Investigadores Publicaciones Libros en coedición Libros de acceso abierto Revistas académicas Eventos Encuentro de investigadores Encuentro de la RIU Concurso de Carteles FIL Guadalajara Simposio Institucional Contacto Buscar Evaluation of dengue virus seroprevalence in four boroughs of Mexico City among persons aged 5-35 years in 2022 Autor/es Anáhuac Coba-Alcalá Eleazar; González-Roldán Jesús Felipe; Ramos-Castañeda José Año de publicación 2025 Journal o Editorial Journal of Infection in Developing Countries Abstract Introduction: Dengue is currently the most widespread vector-borne disease, and its transmission has been intensively studied in endemic/hyperendemic localities. However, to obtain a complete picture of dengue transmission, it is necessary to study nonendemic localities. Imported dengue cases have been reported in Mexico City, and the presence of eggs of the vector Aedes aegyptihas been detected. Methodology: In the present study, we determined the prevalence of IgG antibodies against Dengue virus in four city boroughs via random cluster sampling in individuals aged 5-35 years. Results: The weighted seroprevalence rate was 1.90% (95% CI 0.75-4.75) at Xochimilco, 1.81% (95% CI 0.64-5.00) at Venustiano Carranza, 1.81% (95% CI 0.54-5.83) at Tlahuac, and 5.48% (95% CI 1.96-14.43) at Gustavo A Madero; seropositivity was concentrated in the adult group, many of whom lived in dengue-endemic localities. The distribution of seroprevalence in the four boroughs is very homogeneous and unrelated to the number of vector eggs in the borough. Conclusions: These data suggest that there is still no autochthonous transmission of dengue in Mexico City. However, it is important to note that the structural conditions of the dwellings in these boroughs, which offer minimal barriers to vector infestation, could facilitate the establishment of local transmission under favorable conditions. title: Human challenge study reveals how preexisting immunity affects dengue - News-Medical

content_title: Human challenge study reveals how preexisting immunity affects dengue
content: Dengue virus is especially pernicious compared with many other viruses, as secondary infections can actually be worse than the first one. Now, a new phase 1 trial involving controlled infections in volunteers provides a treasure trove of details about how preexisting immunity and anti-dengue antibodies affect the nature of secondary infections with dengue. The findings are among the first to glean insights using a large controlled human challenge, and could inform future therapeutics and the design of more broadly protective vaccines. Secondary infections with dengue are often the most severe ones, as preexisting antibodies can boost viral counts and raise the risk of severe symptoms. This has frustrated the development of badly needed vaccines for dengue. Furthermore, it's been challenging to understand how pre-infection affects dengue outcomes, as animal models have many limitations and patients usually don't present until after viral counts have peaked. In this study, Camila Odio and colleagues recruited 45 healthy adults who had either zero, one, or more than one prior infection with any of the four strains of dengue virus (DENV1-DENV4). The volunteers received injections of a live, weakened strain of DENV3 in a challenge study, allowing the researchers to fully interrogate dengue immunity dynamics in humans in a safe and controlled setting. The team made various discoveries: for example, they found that people whose antibodies boosted the replication of the virus had the highest viral counts and waning of CD8-bearing T cells and antibodies. Meanwhile, people who had higher amounts of antibodies against the viral nonstructural protein 1 displayed more balanced immune responses and lower viral counts. "Collectively, this work confirms multiple hypotheses generated by natural history studies and reveals the optimal conditions for inducing potent and persistent immunity against DENV1 to DENV4," Odio et al. conclude. Source: Journal reference: Odio, C. D., et al . (2026). Dengue virus controlled human challenge reveals that preexisting immunity shapes viral replication and broadly protective responses. Science Translational Medicine. DOI: 10.1126/scitranslmed.aei5117. https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/scitranslmed.aei5117

title: A 23-year-old with no underlying conditions went into dengue shock and required 13 days of intensive care before ECMO was removed. - Vietnam.vn

content_title: A 23-year-old with no underlying conditions went into dengue shock and required 13 days of intensive care before ECMO was removed.
content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home Culture – Society Y tế A 23-year-old with no underlying conditions went into dengue shock and required 13 days of intensive care before ECMO was removed. Despite having no underlying medical conditions, the young man still went into dengue hemorrhagic shock, suffering severe lung damage that required ECMO and dialysis to maintain his vital functions. Báo Khoa học và Đời sống•26/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 SpO2 dropped to 80%, causing shock and critical respiratory failure despite the patient being young and having no underlying medical conditions. According to Dr. Pham Van Phuc, Deputy Director of the Intensive Care Unit at the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases, patient LTS (23 years old, residing in Tuyen Quang ) had no prior recorded underlying medical conditions. The patient developed a high fever and abdominal pain, and self-medicated at home without improvement. On the third day, the patient experienced frequent loose stools, nausea, and fatigue. After being taken to a nearby medical facility, the patient was diagnosed with dengue fever and treated with intravenous fluids. However, the condition continued to worsen with symptoms of extreme fatigue, agitation, hypotension, and respiratory failure. The patient required intubation and mechanical ventilation before being transferred to the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases. Patients receiving care at the hospital - Photo courtesy of the hospital. Upon admission, the patient was in critical condition. Despite invasive mechanical ventilation with 100% oxygen, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) was only about 80%. Heart rate was rapid at 120–140 beats/minute, blood pressure was 80/40 mmHg despite the use of vasopressors. The patient was cyanotic, had cold extremities, and bilateral pulmonary hypoventilation. Test results showed a positive Dengue test, along with abnormal liver, kidney, and coagulation function. The patient was diagnosed with Dengue hemorrhagic shock, critical respiratory failure progressing to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and suspected gastrointestinal infection. According to Dr. Phuc, this is a particularly severe case of dengue fever in a young person with no underlying health conditions, presenting with shock and severe lung damage, directly threatening their life. Given the patient's oxygen saturation did not improve despite mechanical ventilation at maximum oxygen concentration, the doctors decided to implement extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) to support gas exchange. Simultaneously, the patient received vasopressors, continuous hemodialysis, and resuscitation measures to support circulation, control metabolic disorders, balance fluids, and support kidney function. The patient is being kept alive using ECMO - Photo courtesy of the hospital. After 13 days of intensive care, the patient was weaned off ECMO. By 3 PM on October 26th, after 13 days of intensive treatment at the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases, patient LTS's condition had improved significantly. The patient had been weaned off ECMO and the endotracheal tube, is now conscious, and continues to be monitored and cared for at the hospital. You may also like The patient is expected to be discharged on October 27th if their health remains stable and they meet the discharge criteria. From a state of dengue hemorrhagic shock and critical respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation with maximum oxygen concentration, the patient gradually recovered after a prolonged intensive resuscitation process. This case demonstrates that dengue fever can be severe even in young people without underlying medical conditions. Early detection of warning signs and timely access to treatment are crucial in limiting the risk of serious complications. The fever subsiding does not mean the dangerous phase is over. According to Dr. Phuc, dengue fever is an infectious disease caused by the dengue virus, primarily transmitted through Aedes mosquitoes. The disease can affect people of all ages. Most people recover, but some cases can become severe due to plasma leakage, leading to shock, severe bleeding, and organ damage. The critical phase usually occurs from the 3rd to the 7th day of the illness, especially when the patient's fever begins to subside or has just disappeared. This is when plasma leakage, blood concentration, thrombocytopenia, and shock can occur. Therefore, patients should not be complacent when they see their body temperature drop. Doctors examine patients after the critical stage - Photo courtesy of the hospital. Dr. Phuc advises people to seek medical attention immediately if they experience warning signs such as severe or persistent abdominal pain, frequent vomiting, extreme fatigue, restlessness, lethargy, unusual bleeding, decreased urination, or difficulty breathing. Individuals suspected of having dengue fever should not self-administer intravenous fluids at home or use aspirin, ibuprofen, and other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) due to the risk of increased bleeding. Fluid replacement, fever reduction medication, and laboratory monitoring should be administered according to the instructions of healthcare professionals. Currently, the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases is treating 18 dengue fever patients. Besides early detection of worsening symptoms, people need to proactively eliminate mosquito breeding grounds, cover water containers tightly, kill mosquito larvae, and prevent mosquito bites. Understanding dengue fever vaccination should also be based on age, indications, and current professional guidelines. Symptoms of dengue fever that require immediate medical attention. - Severe or persistent abdominal pain. You may also like - Frequent vomiting, extreme fatigue. - Struggling, sluggish. - Abnormal bleeding. - Infrequent urination or difficulty breathing. (WWSB) - A mosquito-borne illness typically associated with tropical regions is reaching new highs in Florida. And now, there’s one confirmed case in Manatee County. According to the Florida Department of Health’s latest data, more than 400 cases of locally acquired dengue fever have been reported across the state this year. Dengue is a viral infection spread to humans through the bite of an infected mosquito. Christopher Lesser, director of the Manatee County Mosquito Control District, says the district has been taking preventative measures in areas where the disease is more likely to occur. “We’ve been treating our urban areas where this disease normally occurs, once every two weeks. This would be all of Palmetto, all of Bradenton, as a preventative measure,” Lesser said. Lesser says the district has been working to keep mosquito populations low amid a broader dengue outbreak across the Tampa Bay area. He says the mosquito population in urban areas has remained particularly low over the past several months. The mosquito species most commonly associated with spreading dengue, Aedes aegypti, is not common in Manatee County. However, Lesser says residents should remain cautious about mosquito-borne illnesses and mosquito bites in general. So far, there have been no reported cases of locally acquired dengue fever in Sarasota County. Jackie Lebouitz, a chemical in the environment agent with UF/IFAS Extension Sarasota County, says residents should know what symptoms to watch for. Many people who contract dengue do not develop symptoms. For those who do, symptoms can include headaches, fatigue, muscle soreness and, sometimes, a rash. Lebouitz says there are also simple steps people can take to reduce their risk of being bitten. She recommends wearing light-colored, loose-fitting clothing, including long sleeves and pants. She also advises using an EPA-registered insect repellent on exposed skin. While local mosquito control officials continue working to keep mosquito populations down, experts say personal prevention remains an important part of reducing the risk of infection. title: Autoimmune disease linked to greater dengue severity in Colombian cohort
excerpt: A retrospective Colombian cohort of 171 patients found that autoimmune disease was associated with about twice the adjusted odds of severe dengue.

content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, October 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Autoimmune disease linked to greater dengue severity in Colombian cohort by October 26, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Autoimmune disease linked to greater dengue severity in Colombian cohort Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram The study included 171 participants whose outcomes were assessed over 2014–2024: 57 had autoimmune diseases and 114 did not. Severe dengue occurred in 7.0% of the autoimmune-disease group, compared with 2.6% of the comparison group. After adjustment for potential confounders, the association between autoimmune disease and dengue severity was estimated at an odds ratio of 2.14, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.08–4.41 and p = 0.030. The researchers compared demographic, clinical and outcome measures between the two groups and examined laboratory-test trends before, during and after infection. Women represented 87.7% of the sample, and the median age was 48 years. Among participants with autoimmune diseases, rheumatoid arthritis was the most frequent diagnosis at 42%, followed by systemic lupus erythematosus at 29.8% and Sjögren’s syndrome at 19.3%. Patients with autoimmune diseases more often presented with dengue warning signs: these were reported in 66.7% of the autoimmune-disease group and 55.4% of the group without autoimmune diseases. The study also found a higher proportion reporting a previous dengue infection in the autoimmune-disease group, at 49.1% compared with 43.0%. Hospitalization was more frequent among participants with autoimmune disease, at 68.4% versus 61.4%, but that difference was not statistically significant, with p = 0.368. Intensive-care admission was also numerically higher in the autoimmune-disease group, at 12.3% versus 5.3%, although the difference did not reach statistical significance, with p = 0.125. Participants with autoimmune diseases had longer hospital stays, but the supplied research summary does not report the numerical durations. For the severity analysis, the investigators calculated crude and adjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals to identify factors associated with dengue severity. They also performed sensitivity analyses, interaction testing and bootstrap validation, and reported that the findings were consistent across the adjusted, sensitivity and bootstrap analyses. The authors described this consistency as support for the robustness of the association within the dataset. Dengue is an acute viral illness transmitted by the mosquitoes Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus and is prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions. Although most infections are asymptomatic, severe disease can develop, particularly in people with risk factors. The researchers noted that the clinical course of dengue had been studied less extensively in patients with autoimmune diseases and that no prior research on this question had been conducted in Colombia. Larger prospective multicenter studies were needed to confirm the association and clarify its immunopathogenic basis. content: Eighteen people hospitalized with dengue fever, 23-year-old man requires mechanical ventilation. After five days of high fever, abdominal pain, and digestive disorders, the 23-year-old man went into shock and suffered critical respiratory failure. VietNamNet • 26/10/2026 On October 26th, the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases ( Hanoi ) reported that it is currently treating 18 dengue fever patients. Notably, patient LTS (23 years old, residing in Tuyen Quang), who had no prior medical conditions, is in critical condition. Mr. S. developed a high fever and abdominal pain, and self-medicated at home without improvement. On the third day, he experienced frequent loose stools, nausea, and fatigue. After being taken to a nearby medical facility, he was diagnosed with dengue fever and treated with intravenous fluids. However, his condition continued to worsen, developing agitation, hypotension, and respiratory failure, requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation before being transferred to a higher-level facility. Khám phá thêm Tìm hiểu lịch sử Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch Khám phá ĐNA Upon admission to the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases, Mr. S. was in critical condition, his entire body was cyanotic, his extremities were cold, and he had reduced ventilation in both lungs. The patient was admitted to the emergency room in critical condition. Photo: Provided by the hospital. You may also like Ha Tinh province is reorganizing and restructuring units under the Department of Health. (Baohatinh.vn) - The People's Committee of Ha Tinh province has just approved the Project on rearranging and reorganizing units under the Department of Health in the direction of streamlining the organizational structure, effectively utilizing resources, and improving the quality of medical examination and treatment. Is it better to measure blood pressure in the morning or at night? What does a doctor advise? In healthy adults, blood pressure typically drops to its lowest level during deep sleep. Afterward, blood pressure begins to gradually rise about 1-2 hours before waking and is usually higher in the morning. Stroke doesn't discriminate by age: Silent risks people under 45 should be aware of. Stroke is often considered a disease of older adults, but in reality, young people can also experience this event. The cause may be related to risk factors that have silently accumulated over many years. Tests confirmed a positive Dengue test, along with abnormal liver, kidney, and coagulation function. The patient was diagnosed with Dengue hemorrhagic shock, critical respiratory failure progressing to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Given that the patient's blood oxygen levels did not improve despite mechanical ventilation at maximum oxygen concentration, The doctors decided to implement extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) to support respiration. The patient was also given vasopressors, continuous hemodialysis, and close monitoring of organ function. According to Dr. Pham Van Phuc, Deputy Director of the Intensive Care Unit at the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases, this was a particularly severe case of dengue fever in a young person with no underlying conditions. The shock and severe lung damage directly threatened the patient's life, requiring a combination of intensive resuscitation measures. You may also like By 3 PM on October 26th, after 13 days of intensive treatment, patient S.'s condition had improved. The patient was weaned off ECMO and the endotracheal tube was removed. The patient is now conscious and continues to be monitored and cared for at the hospital. Based on this case, Dr. Phuc warned that dengue fever can become severe even in young, healthy individuals without underlying conditions. The disease is primarily transmitted through Aedes mosquitoes. In some cases, plasma leakage may occur, leading to shock, severe bleeding, and organ damage. content: Skip to content Wednesday, October 28, 2026 About Us Contact X-twitter Instagram Facebook Home News Eats Sports Lifestyle Real Estate Home News Eats Sports Lifestyle Real Estate 0 Search Home Health » News Dengue cases rise in Florida: What to know about symptoms By Selim Algar on October 23, 2026 on 2:47 pm Updated on: 10/23/2026 Share this post : Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Dr. Hongfei Di of Paradigm Primary Care. Florida added 57 locally acquired dengue cases to its latest weekly tally, and a St. Johns County doctor says recognizing symptoms can help patients know when to get checked. The state has recorded 425 cases acquired in Florida this year, according to the Department of Health’s report for Oct. 11–17. Dr. Hongfei Di, of Paradigm Primary Care and Wellness, said the early symptoms can be misleading. “Dengue fever sounds bad, but the initial presentation is just like your common cold or flu,” Dr. Di said. St. Johns County has recorded three travel-associated dengue cases this year, meaning those people were infected elsewhere. No locally acquired cases have been reported in the county thus far, according to the state report. Most cases have been reported in Hillsborough and Pinellas counties. About one in four people infected with dengue develop symptoms, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Those can include fever, headaches, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint aches, nausea and a rash. Most people who become ill recover after about a week. Dr. Hongfei Di at his Nocatee office. Patients should tell their healthcare provider about recent travel and mosquito exposure, which can help guide evaluation. “When you really do need to seek help is if you have any signs of gum bleeding, nosebleeds, or easily bruising all of a sudden,” Dr. Di said. About one in 20 people who become sick develop severe dengue, according to the CDC. Warning signs include abdominal pain, repeated vomiting and extreme tiredness or restlessness. Those signs commonly appear within 24 to 48 hours after the fever goes away, when patients may think they are recovering. There is no specific medicine to treat dengue. For mild illness, care generally involves rest, fluids and acetaminophen for fever or pain. Using mosquito repellent and emptying standing water around the home can help prevent bites. Paradigm Primary Care and Wellness is an advertising partner of St. Johns Citizen. content: 越南湄公河三角洲地区E-Dengue早期预警系统用于主动登革热防控的经济学评价:一项研究方案 《PharmacoEconomics - Open》:Economic Evaluation of an E-Dengue Early Warning System for Proactive Dengue Prevention in the Mekong Delta Region, Vietnam: A Protocol 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年10月28日 来源:PharmacoEconomics - Open 2.0 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Protocol Open access 摘要 背景:已开发多种登革热早期预警工具,但少有成功整合至常规监测系统。E-Dengue工具依据“Useful, Usable, and Used”框架设计,旨在预测越南湄公河三角洲地区(MDR)提前3个月的登革热流行。该方案概述一种早期预警系统的经济学评价,其中E-Dengue预警触发主动登革热防控干预。 方法:将开展基于社会视角的经济学评价,并与整群随机对照试验(cRCT)并行。比较E-Dengue早期预警系统与常规实践的成本和结局。主要结局指标为伤残调整生命年(DALYs),次要结局指标为登革热病例数。通过疾病成本子研究(cost-of-illness substudy)量化登革热病例的平均成本,该子研究利用医院账单记录、对患者和非正式照护者的结构化调查以及文献证据综合。E-Dengue的成本效果将在2年时间范围内评估,分别表示为每避免1个DALY和每避免1例登革热病例的增量成本,并与预设成本效果阈值比较。采用单因素和概率敏感性分析(one-way and probabilistic sensitivity analyses)评估结果稳健性。 讨论:证明E-Dengue具有成本效果,将为支持其整合至MDR常规监测提供严格证据,并可能支持其在越南其他地区和条件相似国家推广和适配。反之,若E-Dengue不具成本效果,该研究将为未来早期预警工具的设计和实施提供关键教训。 试验注册号:ACTRN12626000402347。 论文解读:原文为一项健康经济学评价方案,未报告实证结果。登革热(dengue)由Aedes蚊传播,在热带和亚热带国家负担高;气候变化、全球流动和城市化使全球发病率显著上升,东南亚在发病率、死亡率和伤残调整生命年(DALYs,disability-adjusted life years)上受影响最重。越南登革热年报告病例波动明显,2021—2025年报告数从69,140至345,234不等,且因无症状或轻症漏报,估计总病例为442,911—2,603,443,经济负担为US$29.77 million—US$94.87 million(2016价格);湄公河三角洲地区(MDR,Mekong Delta Region)发病率最高。现有媒介控制以化学、生物和/或环境管理为主,无单一措施优于其他,联合干预最有效但时间可持续性有限、需周期性重复;Wolbachia感染蚊释放和登革热疫苗仍需更多有效性、安全性和成本效果证据。早期预警系统(EWS)有潜力,但应用受模型准确性、数据及时性与质量、整合至国家监测系统以及将模型输出转化为行动的能力限制。E-Dengue依据“Useful, Usable, and Used”框架开发,利用流行病学和气候数据在区域卫生中心(RHC,Regional Health Center)水平提前3个月预测流行,并形成用户友好开源软件平台,目标整合入MDR常规监测;因公共资源有限,使用前需量化其价值。研究人员开展与平行组两臂cRCT并行的健康经济学评价,遵循健康经济评价报告规范(CHEERS 2022,Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standard 2022),比较E-Dengue预警触发主动干预与常规实践;主要结局为DALYs,次要结局为登革热病例,采用社会视角和2年时间范围,计算增量成本效果比(ICER,incremental cost-effectiveness ratio),并与预设支付意愿(WTP,willingness-to-pay)阈值比较。原文指出,若具成本效果,可支持整合、优化预算和人力资源并可能推广;若不具成本效果,可为未来EWS设计实施提供教训;若效力不足,可用经验成本数据在不同假设效力下建模;无论结果如何,均可为EWS和数字健康技术评估提供案例证据。 欢迎下载《重组激酶全方位解析:高效生产、严格质控与前沿应用》 领 取 关键技术方法(≤250字):在越南MDR的118个RHC开展两臂平行cRCT,干预臂由E-Dengue提前3个月预警触发主动物理灭源与教育、信息与沟通(EIC,education, information, and communication),非干预臂常规实践并平行开展幼虫调查;采用社会视角成本效果分析,疾病成本子研究在Dong Thap省Dong Thap医院和Cao Lanh综合医院招募135例门诊和135例住院患者及非正式照护者,结合医院账单、结构化问卷和文献综合;以看似无关回归(SUR,seemingly unrelated regression)估计增量成本与DALYs/病例,计算ICER,并行单因素和概率敏感性分析。 研究结果(方案设计):原文为方案,以下为方案规定的分析产出。研究现场:MDR覆盖>40,000 km2、人口17.43 million,行政改革后为五个半省、555 communes、128 RHCs,排除后118 RHCs入组,前Long An地区按地理属MDR纳入。研究设计:在2026和2027年两个登革热季节开展两臂平行cRCT,排除10个RHCs(8个避免污染、2个岛屿)后按59/59随机分配;两臂按越南卫生部指南常规防控,干预臂每月E-Dengue预警触发主动干预和幼虫调查,非干预臂仅幼虫调查;主动干预在预测流行月前1个月于高历史发病communes实施物理灭源(无杀虫剂)和全communes EIC,CDC于灭源前1天、后1天、后3周调查幼虫,非干预臂平行两次间隔4周。成本数据的样本量与抽样:主动活动成本在59个干预RHC、常规活动成本在118个RHC收集;疾病成本子研究在Dong Thap省两家医院作描述性单臂横断面调查,按Johnston et al.公式以V=0.15、Cv=0.75估算n≈97,补偿后目标135例住院和135例门诊及照护者。数据收集:健康结局指标中主要结局DALYs=YLD+YLL,采用0.0307和0.0351残疾权重并考虑33%患者后急性症状平均11.2个月;次要病例数来自常规监测,住院病例用1.2扩展因子校正,按非正式照护64.1%、门诊23.3%、住院12.6%估算;成本估计采用社会视角,以2024年世界银行平均汇率折算美元并用GDP平减指数或CCEMG–EPPI Cost Converter v1.7调整通胀;E-Dengue工具开发与运行成本来自项目、越南国家卫生与流行病学研究所(NIHE,National Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology)等财务报告,设备基础设施按3%折现年化;主动干预成本来自项目/NIHE财务报告;常规登革热控制成本来自省疾病控制中心(CDC,Centers for Disease Control)、两臂收集,人力资源成本仅在Dong Thap省收集;疾病成本在两医院收集直接医疗、直接非医疗和生产力成本,直接医疗取2025年账单,直接非医疗和生产力由护士用结构化问卷访谈,非正式照护按US$17.32/例(2024价格)假设,生产力成本用人力资本和机会成本法。成本效果分析:EpiData/Excel录入、R分析,以RHC水平SUR估计增量成本和健康结局并调整基线协变量,计算ICER;成本不折现、YLL按3%折现、时间2年;基础WTP阈值0.5×人均GDP=US$2533(2025价格),敏感性用0.34×和1×人均GDP,病例结局WTP为每例估计成本;行单因素和概率敏感性(Monte Carlo,DALYs/成本用Gamma分布、病例用Poisson分布)分析,并报告成本效果平面、成本效果可接受性曲线及卫生服务视角分析。伦理批准:访谈前取得书面知情同意,方案获NIHE IRB–07/2023和University of Queensland 2023/HE001441批准。 讨论部分总结:该方案提供可推广至其他病媒传染病EWS的成本效果评价方法;据研究人员所知,这是首个估计任何EWS成本效果的研究,而现有EWS如D-MOSS、DART和EWARS的开发运行成本信息有限。原文指出三项局限:RHC和省工作人员常规防控成本仅在一个省收集,可能高估或低估;无法捕获全部常规防控成本,如志愿社区团队及整体传染病监测成本中归因登革热比例;患者成本来自单一省两家医院,单位成本可能不反映五个半省异质性,研究用单因素(均值±标准差或±25%)和概率敏感性分析处理。政策意义:评估有效性和成本效果对卫生部、CDC及省/commune利益相关者关键;若有效且具成本效果,可支持整合至MDR常规实践,首次引入主动成分以降低成本效果方式减少发病和局部暴发,并优化预算与人力,可能推广至越南其他地区和相似条件地区;若不具成本效果,提示不应常规使用,可能因高成本或缺乏效力;若缺乏效力,可用经验成本数据在不同假设效力下建模;若结果不确定,可进一步识别不确定性驱动因素并开展亚组分析。 研究结论(译文):无论cRCT和成本效果分析结果如何,所积累的证据将有助于政策制定者和实践者评估其他EWS或类似新技术的经济影响。该cRCT及成本效果分析将作为一个重要案例研究,提供与EWS和数字健康技术评估相关的重要证据和经验教训,而当前文献中此类证据仍相对有限。 title: 登革热VS基孔肯雅热:症状对比、传播途径和预防措施
excerpt: 所谓“蚊媒传染病”,就是蚊子在叮咬时把病毒或寄生虫“快递”到人体内的疾病;国内需要重点盯防的有登革热、基孔肯雅热、寨卡病毒病、乙型脑炎和疟疾等。 今天,我们先锁定由伊蚊“投递”的两大热门疾病——登革热与基孔肯雅热。 它是由登革病毒引起的,经伊蚊叮咬传播的虫媒传染病。据世界卫生组织统计,全球每年约有1-4亿人感染,其中美洲、东南亚和西太平洋区域发病最为严重,亚洲约占全球疾病负担的70%。
